scope: Original 2026-10-15 intent preserved; 2026-10-16 approves I in PLA shell and requests thinner I derivatives. Physical feedback retained separately. Later preprint I24/I20 rejection and robust replacements are recorded in README; local-feature thickness must not be conflated with total liner thickness. Latest user directive replaces unprinted I26 with an extreme sample beyond I22; I10 dimensions/topology are agent decisions, not user acceptance thresholds. Latest print feedback accepts I22 quietness, rejects broken I10, and explicitly requires both skins in thinner follow-ups. On 2026-10-17 user requests finish-only 30 mm coupons (four to eight) with solid exterior edges, retaining S16 as damping baseline and deferring physical damping comparison. Full-box intent is preserved; sample plans cannot qualify omitted enclosure coverage. On 2026-10-20 user accepts the two SVG interpretations, authorizes four complete labeled cup/pad pairs (A 1.6/2.0 mm; B 1.6 mm with two tie sizes), and explicitly requires no Arachne. Installation survival remains physical after reported dental-liner breakage. Later on 2026-10-20 the user rejects all four before printing because walls disappear in their slice; requests ordinary Classic compatibility without Arachne. R2 preserves selected total thicknesses while using .5 mm continuous skins and ordinary widths with thin-wall detection off. User clarifies that the failure used defaults as in the repository and authorises increased A thickness if needed. R2 has so far retained the original thicknesses; the exact default diagnostic triplet is also checked for wall generation.

user_requirements.text: One small closable PETG enclosure accepts interchangeable separately printed TPU liners and a loose metal nut.

source.statement: User requests one small PETG exterior, closable, with TPU inserts and space to shake a stock metal nut.

user_requirements.text: The floor, ceiling and all four interior walls have TPU damping coverage.

source.statement: User explicitly requires damping on the bottom, top, and all four walls.

user_requirements.text: All object-contact interior faces are flat; damping structures are inside the liner.

source.statement: User clarification: the interior needs to be flat for the objects, while the liner may have structures inside.

user_requirements.text: Several permanently labeled CAD-defined internal damping configurations can be printed together.

source.statement: User asks for labeled variants, explicit CAD structures rather than infill, and a batch print; additional variants are welcome.

user_requirements.text: Use research to inform a reusable damping experiment and compare variants by shaking the same metal nut.

source.statement: User requests research on effective damping structures and plans to report which liner performs best.

user_requirements.text: Prioritize maximum quietness in a thin liner and recommend a focused print batch with a solid control and the most promising candidates.

source.statement: User follow-up: maximize quietness while keeping it thin; provide a STEP set focused on more confident candidates and retain control A.

user_requirements.text: Thinner follow-up liners retain both continuous inner and outer TPU skins for stable printing.

source.statement: User reports I10 shell-side print damage, says both walls are needed, and requests one or two significantly thinner stable variants; slicer changes are allowed.

user_requirements.text: Provide roughly 30 mm square flat plate samples, four to eight designs printable together, with filled exterior edges.

source.statement: User requests four to eight roughly three-centimetre square bottom-plate samples rather than full boxes, filled exterior overhangs and a flat test face.

user_requirements.text: Explore structures that reduce visible surface lines and waviness beyond the current 50% ironing result.

source.statement: User reports visible surface waviness despite improvement at 50% ironing and requests several internal structure experiments.

user_requirements.text: Keep damping usefulness as a later physical test; S16 remains the preferred baseline.

source.statement: User names S16 as the best so far and says damping must still be tested later while initially focusing on surface texture.

user_requirements.text: All four support-test variants must use Classic, without Arachne.

source.statement: During implementation the user explicitly reiterates: I do not want Arachne.

user_requirements.text: Provide four labeled complete cup/lid-insert pairs for the existing experiment box: A at 1.6 and 2.0 mm; B at 1.6 mm with two distinct tie sizes.

source.statement: User accepts both SVG explanations and requests four printable variants, matching lids and markings: A at 16/20 and B at 16 with two distinct tie sizes; the S16 context establishes 1.6/2.0 mm units.

user_requirements.text: Find a thin liner that survives installation and handling with mutually supported walls and bottom.

source.statement: User reports further dental-liner breakage during insertion and requests support experiments to find the minimum usable thickness without breakage.

user_requirements.text: The four replacements must generate their wall skins with ordinary Classic slicing, without Arachne or dependence on thin-wall recovery.

source.statement: User reports wall paths missing on all four variants, declines printing the batch, and requests investigation and repair for normal slicing without Arachne.

user_requirements.text: The replacements must retain wall paths with the ordinary repository default slicing process.

source.statement: Asked which slicer/nozzle/line width/profile was used for the failure, the user answers: default as in the repo. They allow increased A thickness if needed, prioritising reliable Classic slicing.

surface_publication.review: Current native evaluator rebuilt the selected geometry and associated both exports; artifact identity unchanged from first slice. Only these reviewed source/profile bytes and exports may consume the retained paths. Republish and review before updating this association for a geometry change.
